topic.title: Equivalent fractions
topic.overview: Equivalent fractions are fractions that represent the same value or proportion, even though they may have different numerators and denominators. To find equivalent fractions, multiply or divide both the numerator and denominator of a fraction by the same nonzero number. Changing only the numerator or only the denominator usually changes the value of the fraction. A fraction itself denotes a ratio of the numerator to the denominator.

question.reference_answer: A fraction represents a ratio of the numerator to the denominator, meaning it shows how many parts of a certain size are taken from a whole divided into equal parts. For example, in the fraction 3/4, the numerator 3 indicates three parts, and the denominator 4 indicates that the whole is divided into four equal parts. This means 3/4 represents three out of four equal parts of a whole. Thus, the fraction expresses a ratio between the numerator and denominator, showing a part of a whole or a ratio between two quantities.
